ko.title: 천문단위
ko.description:
**AU는 지구와 태양 사이의 평균 거리에 가까운 고정된 길이 단위다.**

### 거리 계산의 흐름

천문단위를 쓰면 태양계의 큰 거리를 익숙한 기준과 비교하기 쉽다. 1 au는 정확히 149,597,870,700 m로 정해져 있으므로, 1.5 au라는 가상 거리는 약 2억 2440만 km다. 지구가 공전하며 태양에 가까워지거나 멀어져도 자의 길이가 바뀌는 것은 아니다. 평균 지구–태양 거리는 단위를 이해하는 기준이고, 실제 그날의 거리는 별도로 측정하는 양이라는 점을 나누어 생각하면 된다.

### 관측과 예시

1 AU는 약 1억 5천만 km다.

### 구분할 점

실제 지구와 태양의 거리는 공전 중 변한다.

### 그림 안내

거리의 로그 눈금: ① 지구 궤도 반지름 ② 해왕성 궤도 반지름 ③ 태양 다음으로 가까운 항성까지 ④ 우리은하 원반 지름의 대략적 규모. 같은 간격은 같은 거리 배율입니다.

en-US.title: Astronomical unit
en-US.description:
**An AU is a fixed distance close to the mean Earth–Sun separation.**

### How the distance follows

The astronomical unit makes large Solar System distances easier to compare with a familiar scale. One au is defined as exactly 149,597,870,700 meters, so an illustrative separation of 1.5 au is about 224.4 million kilometers. Earth moving closer to or farther from the Sun does not stretch this ruler. The mean Earth–Sun separation helps explain the scale; the actual separation on a particular date is a different quantity to measure.

### Evidence and examples

One AU is about 150 million kilometers.

### Keep in mind

Earth’s actual separation changes during its orbit.

ja.title: 天文単位
ja.description:
**AUは地球と太陽の平均距離に近い固定の長さの単位。**

### 距離を導く流れ

天文単位を使うと太陽系の大きな距離を身近な尺度と比べやすい。1 auは正確に149,597,870,700 mと定義され、例として1.5 auなら約2億2440万kmになる。地球が太陽へ近づいたり遠ざかったりしても物差しは伸縮しない。平均地球–太陽間距離は尺度を理解する目安で、ある日の実際の距離は別に測る量である。

### 観測と例

1 AUは約1億5000万km。

### 注意点

実際の地球と太陽の距離は公転中に変化する。

### 図の説明

距離の対数目盛：①地球の軌道半径 ②海王星の軌道半径 ③太陽を除いて最も近い恒星まで ④銀河円盤の直径の概数。同じ間隔は同じ倍率です。

**광년은 빛이 진공에서 1년 동안 이동하는 거리다.**

en-US.title: Light-year
en-US.description:
**A light-year is the distance light travels through vacuum in one year.**

### How the distance follows

A light-year multiplies a duration by light’s speed to define a length. Using about 9.46 trillion kilometers per light-year, four light-years is about 37.84 trillion kilometers. In a nearby-space example neglecting relative motion and expansion, light crossing that separation takes about four years. The star itself need not be four years old. Its age and the signal’s travel time answer different questions, even though the distance unit contains the word “year.”

### Evidence and examples

It is about 9.46 trillion kilometers.

### Keep in mind

Despite its name, it measures distance, not age.

ja.title: 光年
ja.description:
**光年は光が真空中を1年間に進む距離。**

### 距離を導く流れ

光年は時間に光速を掛けて定める長さである。1光年を約9兆4600億kmとすると、4光年は約37兆8400億kmになる。相対運動と膨張を無視した近傍宇宙の例なら、そこを渡る光には約4年かかる。星自体が4歳という意味ではない。単位に年があっても、星の年齢と信号の移動時間は異なる問いに答える。

### 観測と例

1光年は約9兆4600億km。

### 注意点

年という字があっても年齢ではなく距離を表す。

### 図の説明

en-US.title: Light travel time
en-US.description:
**Light takes time to cross space, so received signals describe an earlier event.**

### How the distance follows

Dividing roughly 149.6 million kilometers by about 299,792 kilometers per second gives 499 seconds, or eight minutes nineteen seconds. Sunlight arriving now left the vicinity of the Sun’s visible surface that much earlier. This calculation does not include the transport of energy through the solar interior to the surface. Distinguishing arrival time from departure time explains why an astronomical observation records an earlier state without requiring the source to have vanished since then.

### Evidence and examples

Sunlight reaches Earth in about eight minutes.

### Keep in mind

A delayed view does not mean the source has stopped existing.

### Sources

- [1](https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/)

ja.title: 光の到達時間
ja.description:
**光が空間を渡るには時間がかかり、届く信号は過去の出来事を伝える。**

### 距離を導く流れ

約1億4960万kmを毎秒約29万9792kmで割ると約499秒、8分19秒になる。今届く日光は太陽の見える表面付近をそれだけ前に出た。この計算は内部から表面へのエネルギー輸送時間を含まない。到着と出発の時刻の区別によって、天体がその後消えたと仮定せずに、観測が過去の状態を記録する理由を理解できる。

### 観測と例

太陽光は約8分で地球に届く。

### 注意点

en-US.title: Stellar parallax
en-US.description:
**A nearby star appears to shift against distant backgrounds when our viewpoint changes.**

### How the distance follows

Alternating eyes while viewing a nearby finger shifts it against a distant background. Stellar parallax uses the same geometric idea with much smaller angles. On the same baseline, a star with annual parallax 0.1 arcsecond is approximately half as distant as one with 0.05 arcsecond. Actual measurements fit the repeating yearly pattern alongside the star’s own proper motion. Not every difference between two sky images is therefore a parallax displacement.

### Evidence and examples

Earth’s orbit supplies separated viewpoints over a year.

### Keep in mind

The apparent shift is not the star moving back and forth.

### 観測と例

地球の公転が1年を通じて異なる観測位置を与える。

見かけのずれは星自身の往復運動ではない。

zh-TW.title: 恆星視差

**觀測位置改變時，近處恆星相對遙遠背景的位置會偏移。**

ko.title: 시차의 기준선
ko.description:
**관측 지점 사이의 간격은 시차 측정의 기하학적 기준이 된다.**

### 거리 계산의 흐름

en-US.title: Parallax baseline
en-US.description:
**The separation between observing positions sets the geometric leverage of a parallax measurement.**

### How the distance follows

Using the full maximum displacement between opposite orbital viewpoints as the annual parallax can introduce a factor-of-two error. In an ideal small-angle example, a full excursion of 0.2 arcsecond means parallax p is 0.1 arcsecond and distance is ten parsecs. The two observing sites span about 2 au, whereas the definition uses the 1-au half-baseline. Actual fitting must account for projection on the sky and orbital geometry rather than applying an arbitrary two-image separation.

### Evidence and examples

Opposite sides of Earth’s orbit are about two AU apart.

### Keep in mind

Annual parallax is the half-angle associated with a one-AU baseline.

ja.title: 視差の基線
ja.description:
**観測位置の間隔は視差測定の幾何学的な基準になる。**

### 距離を導く流れ

### 観測と例

地球軌道の反対側どうしは約2 AU離れる。

### 注意点

年周視差は1 AUの基線に対応する半角である。

### 出典

- [1](https://www.nist.gov/how-do-you-measure-it/how-do-you-measure-distance-moon-planets-stars-and-beyond)

zh-TW.title: 視差基線
zh-TW.description:
**觀測位置之間的間隔提供視差測量的幾何基準。**

### 推得距離的過程

### 觀測與例子

地球軌道相對兩端相距約2 AU。

年周視差是對應1 AU基線的半角。

ko.title: 파섹
ko.description:
**1파섹은 연주시차가 1초각인 거리에 해당한다.**

### 거리 계산의 흐름

1초각은 1도를 3600으로 나눈 작은 각도다. 1 au가 그 각도로 보이는 거리 규모는 약 206,265 au이며 약 3.26광년에 해당한다. 파섹은 시차로 얻은 각도를 바로 거리와 연결하기 편하도록 만든 단위다. 예를 들어 2파섹은 약 6.52광년이므로 단위가 바뀌어도 같은 길이를 설명한다. 이 변환 자체가 별의 운동 속도나 여행에 필요한 시간을 정해 주지는 않는다.

en-US.title: Parsec
en-US.description:
**One parsec corresponds to an annual parallax of one arcsecond.**

### How the distance follows

One arcsecond is one degree divided by 3,600. The distance scale at which 1 au spans that small angle is about 206,265 au, or 3.26 light-years. The conversion alone specifies neither the star’s speed nor a traveler’s journey time; those require information beyond a distance.

### Evidence and examples

A parsec is about 3.26 light-years.

### Keep in mind

It is a distance unit, never a unit of travel speed.

移動速度ではなく距離の単位である。

ko.description:

en-US.title: Inverse-square dimming
en-US.description:
**For isotropic light in transparent static space, flux falls with distance squared.**

### How the distance follows

Imagine the same source energy spreading over a sphere of radius r, whose area grows as r squared. Doubling the radius divides that energy among four times the area, leaving one quarter per unit area; tripling it leaves one ninth. The comparison assumes the same isotropic source and no absorption. Dust or directional emission can change the received brightness for other reasons. The geometric explanation shows why distance matters while also identifying when distance alone is not enough.

### Evidence and examples

Doubling distance makes the received flux one quarter.

Dust and cosmic expansion require additional corrections.

ja.title: 距離の二乗による減光
ja.description:

距離が2倍なら受ける束密度は4分の1。

塵や宇宙膨張には追加の補正が必要。

en-US.title: Standard candle
en-US.description:
**A calibrated luminosity lets astronomers infer distance from received brightness.**

### How the distance follows

For two sources with equal calibrated luminosity and no dust absorption, a measured flux one quarter as large implies twice the distance. That inference requires a way to know the luminosity first, so an arbitrary star is not automatically a standard candle. In practice, calibrated relationships between observable features and luminosity make different examples comparable. An error in the reference luminosity shifts the inferred distance as well. The candle is a measurement standard, not necessarily a class of perfectly identical objects.

### Evidence and examples

Nearby examples anchor the calibration before distant ones are used.

### Keep in mind

A standard candle need not have exactly identical luminosity in every case.

先用附近天體建立基準，再套用到遠方。

每個標準燭光不必具有完全相同的光度。

Repeated brightness measurements reveal the pulsation period.

Dust, chemical composition and Cepheid type affect the calibration.

매우 밝아서 개별 세페이드보다 먼 거리까지 측정한다.

en-US.description:
**Cosmic redshift can be converted into a distance within an expansion model.**

### How the distance follows

For an illustrative nearby-Universe calculation, assume recession speed 7,000 km/s and a Hubble constant of 70 km/s/Mpc. Dividing gives about 100 Mpc. This demonstrates the proportional relation, not a new measurement of the constant. Local motions can alter the inference from an observed redshift. At large redshift, extending the straight-line approximation is inadequate; a cosmological model with an expansion history and a specified definition of distance is required.

For nearby expanding-universe galaxies, recession and distance are approximately proportional.

### Keep in mind

Local motions matter, and distant-universe distance definitions differ.

en-US.title: Lookback time
en-US.description:
**Lookback time is how long the light reaching us has been traveling.**

### How the distance follows

Long-traveling light shows a source as it was when that light left. Because the Universe expanded during the journey, the separation at emission, the length made by multiplying travel time by light speed, and the separation at a common cosmic time now generally differ. A locally constant vacuum light speed can coexist with changing cosmic separations. Inferring lookback time from an observed redshift therefore also needs an expansion model; it is not simply a relabeling of today’s distance.

### Evidence and examples

Distant galaxies show earlier stages of cosmic history.

### Keep in mind

Light travel time multiplied by light speed is not generally today’s separation.

zh-TW.title: 回望時間
zh-TW.description:
**回望時間是現在抵達的光已經旅行多久。**

### 推得距離的過程

旅行越久的光呈現越早出發時的天體。途中宇宙膨脹，因此放光時距離、旅行時間乘光速的長度、現在同一宇宙時刻的距離通常不同。局部真空光速恆定，可與宇宙尺度間隔改變並存。從觀測紅移求回望時間也須膨脹模型，不是把今日距離換名稱而已。

### 觀測與例子

遙遠星系呈現宇宙歷史中更早的階段。

### 注意事項

光行時間乘以光速通常不等於今日的實際間距。

cards.title: 과거를 보는 시간
cards.description:
**되돌아보는 시간은 지금 도착한 빛이 여행한 시간이다.**

### 거리 계산의 흐름

오래 여행한 빛을 받을수록 그 빛이 떠났을 당시의 천체 모습을 보게 된다. 하지만 여행하는 동안 우주가 팽창했으므로 출발 당시 거리, 빛의 이동 시간으로 만든 길이, 지금 같은 우주 시각에서의 거리는 일반적으로 다르다. 빛이 진공에서 일정한 국소 광속으로 움직인다는 사실과 양끝 사이의 우주적 거리가 변한다는 사실이 함께 성립한다. 따라서 관측된 적색편이에서 과거 시간을 구할 때도 팽창 모형이 필요하다.

### 관측과 예시

먼 은하는 우주의 더 이른 역사를 보여 준다.

### 구분할 점

빛의 이동 시간에 광속을 곱해도 일반적으로 현재 거리가 되지는 않는다.

ko.description:
**측정한 거리에는 잡음과 보정 가정에서 생기는 불확실성이 있다.**

### 거리 계산의 흐름

10파섹 부근의 추정에 약 1파섹 규모의 불확실성이 있는데 계산기에 10.0000이라고 표시되었다고 해도 정보가 더 정밀해진 것은 아니다. 같은 장비로 반복 관측하면 무작위 잡음을 줄일 수 있지만, 공통 영점 오차가 있다면 반복만으로 없어지지 않는다. 그래서 다른 장비나 방법의 기준과 비교한다. 수치와 함께 어떤 오차를 포함했고 어떤 보정 가정을 썼는지 읽어야 두 거리 추정이 실제로 일치하는지 판단할 수 있다.

### 관측과 예시

독립적인 측정법으로 거리 척도의 일관성을 검사한다.

### 구분할 점

소수 자릿수가 많다고 더 정확한 거리는 아니다.

en-US.title: Distance uncertainty
en-US.description:
**A measured distance includes uncertainty from noise and calibration assumptions.**

### How the distance follows

An estimate near ten parsecs with uncertainty on the order of one parsec does not become more precise because a calculator displays 10.0000. Repeating observations can reduce random noise, but a shared zero-point error does not vanish through repetition alone. Comparisons with other instruments or methods check different aspects of the scale. Read the stated uncertainties and calibration assumptions with the number before deciding whether two distance estimates agree; extra digits are not extra evidence.

### Evidence and examples

Independent methods can test whether a distance scale is consistent.

### Keep in mind

More decimal places do not guarantee a more accurate distance.

ja.description:
**測定距離には雑音や較正の仮定による不確かさがある。**

### 距離を導く流れ

約10パーセクで不確かさが1パーセク程度なら、計算機の10.0000表示で精密さは増えない。反復はランダム雑音を減らせても、共通のゼロ点誤差は反復だけで消えない。別装置や方法との比較が尺度の違う面を点検する。二推定の一致を判断するには値と共に含まれる誤差や校正仮定を読む。桁の追加は根拠の追加ではない。

### 観測と例

独立した方法で距離尺度の整合性を検証できる。

### 注意点

小数点以下の桁数が多くても精度が高いとは限らない。

zh-TW.title: 距離不確定度
zh-TW.description:
**測得的距離包含雜訊與校準假設造成的不確定度。**

### 推得距離的過程

估計約10秒差距、不確定性約1秒差距，計算機顯示10.0000也不會更精確。反覆觀測能減少隨機雜訊，但共通零點誤差不會僅因重複而消失；其他儀器或方法可檢查尺度的不同面向。判斷兩估計是否一致，須連同數字讀誤差範圍與校正假設。多小數位不是多證據。

### 觀測與例子

獨立方法可以檢驗距離尺度是否一致。

### 注意事項

更多小數位不保證距離更準確。
